parsed.explanation: The combined regime is dominated by the federal entry apparatus, which reaches every trans visitor at every port in this state: officers are instructed to refuse cases where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex, and suspicion of misrepresentation can support a permanent lifetime ineligibility finding. Multiple governments have issued trans-specific advisories after detentions. Custody is the severity escalator: immigration detention documents forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse of trans men, and the corrections bureau has adopted conversion-style policies. Inside the state there is no public-accommodations, employment or hate-crime protection for gender identity, SB79 declares an immutable binary and permits sex-segregated spaces, school facility use is tied to birth certificate, and gender-affirming care for under-19s is a felony. No criminalisation of adult trans identity or expression is documented, and no trans-specific violence record is usable, which keeps this out of the lowest tiers.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require sex assigned at birth on passports/visas; X markers discontinued for new issues; officers instructed to refuse cases where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex, with possible permanent lifetime ineligibility under the fraud ground; trans-athlete entry ban; at least eight governments issued trans-specific advisories after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; 'reasonable doubt' standard and non-automatic ineligibility with limited waivers; passport policy under active national litigation.
entry_documents.interaction: Encountered at every airport and port in the state; a mismatch can cascade from secondary inspection to refusal of entry, retention of documents, or detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documented: trans men subjected to forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; national corrections bureau adopted conversion-style policies including hormone removal and forced haircuts; trans prisoner counts no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; several executive measures enjoined in court; no documented traveler-facing custody safeguard.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border document dispute is the pathway by which a visitor enters this system; state and federal placement follows birth sex.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Public school bathroom use tied to birth certificate (HB322); a 2024 university bathroom bill of unresolved status; SB79 declares an immutable binary and permits separate single-sex spaces where privacy, safety or fairness are implicated; national map places the state in ban groupings.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No statewide public-accommodations protection; two municipal ordinances cover residents only; no documented inclusive facility policy.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility and custody rules plus state permissive segregation mean an outed visitor in a state building or lockup is placed by birth sex.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for anyone under 19 is a Class C felony (10 years) for providers, enforceable since 2023; no insurance-exclusion ban; no trans-inclusive state employee benefits; national funding freeze and proposed reimbursement bars.
care_services.interaction: A travelling adult with a trans minor cannot obtain care in-state, and a parent risks service refusal; emergency-care discrimination for visitors is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: SB79 codifies an immutable male-female binary; national counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for prioritised neutralisation; state hate-crime law excludes gender identity, so bias crimes against trans victims lack state coverage.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National 2009 hate-crime statute covers gender identity; gender identity applied to sex under employment law in this circuit since 2011.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises social licence for hostility while state recourse for a trans victim of bias crime is absent.

minors_guardians.exposure: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces a state where care for under-19s is a felony, school sports and bathrooms are assigned by birth certificate, and the family's documents may draw border scrutiny under the sex-doubt cable.
minors_guardians.interaction: State care ban and federal entry screening compound: the minor cannot be treated in-state and the family's records become the adjudication question.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide nondiscrimination or gender-identity hate-crime coverage; polling places the state among the least supportive; no documented trans-specific violence incident or usable rate for this state.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; two municipal ordinances; general rule-of-law functioning.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A trans visitor assaulted or refused service has no state bias-crime or accommodations route, only federal.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The 2024 university bathroom bill's enactment status is unresolved; whether SB79 is applied to adult visitors in state buildings is unresolved; passport-marker litigation is pending; the state's 'legislatively-erasing' grouping rests on unverified bill text.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ on document rules; national civil-liberties litigation; national hate-crime statute.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Practical exposure turns on which federal measures are in force and how state officials read SB79 at the moment of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor denies entry after invasive protocol but has an explicit regulatory bar on detention for marker discrepancies. This jurisdiction has no such bar, adds a possible lifetime ineligibility finding, and its detention system documents abuse, placing it below.

That anchor shows actual custody, phone confiscation, coercion and humiliation, with release. Here custody harm is documented as more severe (forced labour, sexual abuse) but is not shown to be routine at the border, so this jurisdiction sits somewhat above, not at, that tier.

That anchor has a functioning guideline that resolves the discrepancy and issues a valid permit. Here no operative remedy exists: refusal is directed by cable and recourse depends on unresolved national litigation.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime the traveller meets is layered: federal entry screening is the universal exposure, triggered by any document mismatch and capable of refusal, document retention, permanent ineligibility, and — the severity driver — placement in an immigration custody system where abuse of trans detainees is documented. Inside the state, the traveller finds no public-accommodations, employment or bias-crime recourse for gender identity, a statutory declaration of immutable binary sex authorising sex-segregated spaces, school facility rules keyed to birth certificates, and a felony care ban reaching any accompanying minor. Absent documented criminalisation of adult trans identity, documented police targeting, or a usable trans-specific violence record, this sits in the high-risk band rather than the severe tiers.
